quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When weather or light conditions require you to use your lights while driving, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights
High beams
Low beams

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beam light reflects back and creates glare, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as cars
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car
They brake more slowly than cars

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both drivers in danger. You need space and time to avoid a crash if the motorcyclist stops suddenly.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: About the same speed as the freeway traffic
The legal speed limit
A slower speed than the freeway traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: About the same speed as the freeway traffic
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the legal speed limit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merge
Winding road ahead
Reserved parking for people with disabilities

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body.

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating high-fat foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can remove alcohol from your body and reduce its effects.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days to:

options.text: Keep your engine warm
Make it easier for others to see your vehicle
Warn others about bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see your vehicle
questions.explanation: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days, other drivers cannot see your vehicle easily. Use your low beam headlights to make your vehicle visible. If you use windshield wipers, you must also use low beam headlights.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes
Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop until it passes
questions.explanation: Pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. Park parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move to the nearest edge.

questions.question: Stopping distances and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as a vehicle goes faster
Are not affected by a vehicle's speed
Increase as a vehicle goes faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as a vehicle goes faster
questions.explanation: Higher speed increases stopping distance and crash severity. As speed increases, the chance of serious injury and death also increases. Increase your following distance at higher speeds.

questions.question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, you should:

options.text: Keep your headlights on low beam
Use high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle
Use high beams

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlights on low beam
questions.explanation: Use high beams only in rural areas when no other cars are nearby. Use low beams when following another vehicle closely.

questions.question: Driving slower than surrounding traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather
Okay if you don't know the speed limit
Often a hazard because frustrated drivers may try to pass unsafely

questions.correctAnswerText: Often a hazard because frustrated drivers may try to pass unsafely
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. Drivers behind you may get impatient and take risks to pass you.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have larger blind spots than most cars. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians who use guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and makes it harder to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing or symbols.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Slow down and let vehicles and pedestrians cross your path before you proceed. Stop if necessary.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is prohibited from both directions.
Passing is permitted from both directions.
Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.
questions.explanation: Only drivers next to the dashed line may cross the centerline to pass. Drivers next to the solid line may not pass.

questions.question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle:

options.text: Beep your horn.
Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
Expect the unexpected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Children on bicycles are unpredictable and may change direction suddenly. Children and bicycles are small and hard to see.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed on the road.
The road narrows ahead.
There is a series of curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions immediately ahead. This sign warns you about a winding road.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing to the right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
May turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. It frustrates drivers behind you, who may make risky moves to pass. Drive with traffic flow, within the speed limit.

questions.question: A police officer directs you to go through a red traffic light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection without stopping.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection without stopping.
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions always override traffic signals and signs. Follow the officer's instructions.

questions.question: Your tire suddenly goes flat while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal rapidly several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep straight. Remove your foot from the gas. Do not brake. Let the car slow on its own. Brake gently only if needed. Pull to the side of the road when safe.

questions.question: You arrive at a four-way stop at the same time as the driver on your left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on your left.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at a four-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: You have a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can do so safely.

questions.question: At a yield sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic close enough to cause a problem.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic close enough to cause a problem.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic in the lanes you want to enter or cross. Be ready to stop, but you can continue if there is no traffic.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked position, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap to match the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap to match the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or slope.
When parked on a flat roadside with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or slope.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight so a rear-end hit won't push you into oncoming traffic. On a hill, angle wheels away from traffic so the vehicle won't roll if brakes fail.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Check your blind spot over your shoulder.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always signal before changing lanes. This gives other drivers time to react.

questions.question: To see objects in your blind spot when changing lanes, you should check:

options.text: Only the left mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only the rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the correct shoulder to check your blind spot when changing lanes.
